title: Interleave the Two Halves
statement:
You get an array nums of length 2n and the number n. The first half is x₀, x₁, …, xₙ₋₁ and the second half is y₀, y₁, …, yₙ₋₁.

Return a new array that alternates between the halves, taking from the first half first: [x₀, y₀, x₁, y₁, …, xₙ₋₁, yₙ₋₁].

examples.why: The halves are [4, 8, 1] and [6, 2, 9]. Take 4, then 6, then 8, then 2, and so on.
One item per half: nothing moves.
The partner of position i is i + n, not i + 1: interleaving neighbours would leave the array unchanged.

gen: (r, big) => { const n = big ? 50000 : r.int(1, 6); return [r.arr(2 * n, 1, 1000), n]; }
hints: Where does the partner of nums[i] live, for i in the first half?
It is at index i + n. Output positions 2i and 2i + 1 get nums[i] and nums[i + n].
One loop over i from 0 to n − 1 fills the whole result.

explain.intuition:
This is a zipper. The two halves are the two sides, and each tooth on the left (nums[i]) meets the matching tooth on the right (nums[i + n]). Writing them to positions 2i and 2i + 1 of a new array closes the zipper in one pass.

It is the same move as merging two equal-length columns of a table into one alternating list, as you might do to show "question, answer, question, answer".
steps: For i from 0 to n − 1: set out[2i] = nums[i] and out[2i + 1] = nums[i + n].
pitfalls: Pairing nums[i] with nums[i + 1]. That pairs neighbours, not the two halves.
Starting with the second half. The first item of the result is x₀.

solutions.title: Index math in one pass
solutions.idea: Position 2i takes nums[i]; position 2i + 1 takes nums[i + n].

solutions.title: In place by packing pairs
solutions.idea: Values are at most 1000 < 1024, so each slot can hold two values: the x in the low 10 bits and the y above it. Pack each pair into the first half, then unpack from the back.

followups: Do it in place with O(1) extra space when values are not bounded. (Hint: follow the cycles of the permutation.)
Undo it: given the interleaved array, rebuild the two halves.
